title: Model Generation Method for Optimising Fire Protection Thickness
author: Li, Feng, et al.

steps.title: Replace .rpy commands with explicit methods
steps.instruction: Use the kernel scripting interface to substitute the .rpy machine‑code commands with explicit variable‑based functions such as getClosest(), getByBoundingBox() and getByBoundingCylinder() so that model parameters can be directly accessed and modified.

steps.title: Define model variables and geometry
steps.instruction: Create variables for all modelling parameters: section dimensions, insulation thickness, insulation conductivity, mesh size, lower‑flange target temperature, and allowable temperature residual; then use these variables in the ABAQUS script to generate the 3‑side protection steel‑beam model.

steps.title: Establish interaction region and tie constraints
steps.instruction: Call getByBoundingBox() to define the interaction region, adding a 0.01 mm allowance to the selection to avoid errors; provide at least one maximum or minimum XYZ coordinate and avoid including unconnected edges to reduce edge arrays; use the same method to create tie constraints between the steel and the fire‑protection elements.

steps.title: Create reusable model‑generation function
steps.instruction: Wrap the entire model‑building sequence—including variable definitions, interaction region creation, tie constraints, and partitioning of the steel‑fire‑protection junction—into a Python function so it can be called repeatedly for optimisation studies.

steps.title: Set mesh size and partition junction
steps.instruction: Assign the mesh size as a variable that scales with the section dimensions; partition the faces at the steel‑fire‑protection junction using the GUI‑generated scripts to obtain a uniform mesh across the geometry.

steps.title: Create node set for temperature output
steps.instruction: Use getByBoundingBox() again to generate a node set that contains all nodes of the lower flange; this node set will be used later to extract temperature values. The temperature degree of freedom for solid sections is NT11.

steps.title: Run simulation with timing safeguards
steps.instruction: Submit the ABAQUS job and wait for its completion; insert time.sleep calls between heavy computational steps such as mesh generation to prevent job jams and to refresh terminal messages. Replace the total analysis time with the variable ‘target time’ for computational efficiency.

steps.title: Extract temperature data before target time
steps.instruction: Set the target temperature as the maximum temperature of the lower flange. Use xyDataListfromfield() to obtain temperature data, which returns a three‑layer list; index it as [0][i][0] where 0 = data output, i = time‑frame number, and the final 0 = step time. Limit extraction to frames occurring before the target time by employing a timeframe object as a frame repository.

steps.title: Obtain maximum lower‑flange temperature
steps.instruction: Apply getSubset() to the temperature object of all lower‑flange nodes, then iterate with a ‘for’ loop to collect object.data into a Python list and compute the maximum value with the built‑in max() function.

steps.title: Adjust insulation thickness based on temperature criteria
steps.instruction: When modifying the insulation thickness, ensure that the resulting maximum lower‑flange temperature is either higher than the target temperature or lower than (Tlimit – σT); repeat the model‑generation and analysis steps until this condition is satisfied.
